title.en: Binomial theorem for a positive integral index

title.en: Expand binomials with signs and fractions

say.en: Writing Pascal's triangle down to row 20 is slow. The binomial theorem gives any row at once using to the power nC r. In this lesson: State the binomial theorem.
Expand binomials with signs and fractions.

body.en: For any *positive* integer $n$: $(a + b)^n = {}^nC_0 a^n + {}^nC_1 a^{n-1}b + {}^nC_2 a^{n-2}b^2 + \dots + {}^nC_n b^n$. There are $n + 1$ terms; the index of $a$ falls by 1 and the index of $b$ rises by 1 from term to term, and in each term the indices add up to $n$. For $(a - b)^n$ the signs alternate.
body.kn: (a + b)ⁿ = Σ ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ, r = 0 ಯಿಂದ n ವರೆಗೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಪದದಲ್ಲಿ ಘಾತಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ n. (a − b)ⁿ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಚಿಹ್ನೆಗಳು ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Indices in each term add up to n

narration.en: a plus b to the power n is the sum of n C r times a to the n minus r times b to the r, for r from zero to n. The powers in each term add up to n, and for a minus b the signs alternate.
narration.kn: (a + b)ⁿ = Σ ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ, r = 0 ಯಿಂದ n ವರೆಗೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಪದದಲ್ಲಿ ಘಾತಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ n. (a − b)ⁿ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಚಿಹ್ನೆಗಳು ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Square of a sum, and beyond

narration.en: A square of side a + b splits into a², two ab rectangles and b², so (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². For a higher index n the coefficients ⁿC₀, ⁿC₁, … come from Pascal's triangle; the terms always add up to (a + b)ⁿ.
narration.kn: a + b ಬಾಹುವಿನ ಚೌಕ a², ಎರಡು ab ಆಯತಗಳು ಮತ್ತು b² ಆಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಘಾತ n ಗೆ ಗುಣಾಂಕಗಳು ⁿC₀, ⁿC₁, … ಪಾಸ್ಕಲ್ ತ್ರಿಭುಜದಿಂದ; ಪದಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ (a + b)ⁿ.

say.en: A square of side a plus b splits into a squared, two ab rectangles and b squared, so a plus b squared equals a squared plus 2ab plus b squared. For a higher index n the coefficients to the power nC 0, to the power nC 1,... come from Pascal's triangle; the terms always add up to a plus b to the power n.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Expand (x² + 3/x)⁴, x ≠ 0.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Expand (x squared plus 3 over x) to the power 4, x is not equal to 0.
Coefficients 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 with a equals x squared, b equals 3 over x.
x to the power 8 plus 4x to the power 6(3 over x) plus 6x to the power 4(9 over x squared) plus 4x squared(27 over x cubed) plus 81 over x to the power 4.
Simplify each term.
So the answer is x to the power 8 plus 12x to the power 5 plus 54x squared plus 108 over x plus 81 over x to the power 4.

steps.en: In the difference, terms with even powers of √2 cancel and odd ones double.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Evaluate (√3 + √2)⁴ − (√3 − √2)⁴.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Evaluate (the square root of 3 plus the square root of 2) to the power 4 - (the square root of 3 - the square root of 2) to the power 4.
In the difference, terms with even powers of the square root of 2 cancel and odd ones double.
= 2[ to the power 4C 1the square root of 3 cubedthe square root of 2 plus to the power 4C 3the square root of 3the square root of 2 cubed] = 2[12 the square root of 6 plus 8 the square root of 6].
So the answer is 40 the square root of 6.

heading.en: Sum and difference of conjugate powers

body.en: (a + b)ⁿ + (a − b)ⁿ keeps only the odd-numbered terms (even powers of b), doubled. (a + b)ⁿ − (a − b)ⁿ keeps only the even-numbered terms (odd powers of b), doubled.

narration.en: Sum and difference of conjugate powers. (a + b)ⁿ + (a − b)ⁿ keeps only the odd-numbered terms (even powers of b), doubled. (a + b)ⁿ − (a − b)ⁿ keeps only the even-numbered terms (odd powers of b), doubled.

mnemonic.en: Plus keeps even powers of b; minus keeps odd

say.en: Sum and difference of conjugate powers. a plus b to the power n plus (a - b) to the power n keeps only the odd-numbered terms even powers of b, doubled. a plus b to the power n - (a - b) to the power n keeps only the even-numbered terms odd powers of b, doubled.
